hypothesis: An hour of extreme net taker buying (selling) on the Binance perp, when the perp premium has NOT already been pushed to an extreme in the same direction, is followed by a same-direction drift over the next 12h; trading it beats side-matched random twins on the same entries and brackets.
mechanism: Large traders split orders, so aggressive imbalances are autocorrelated and lagged imbalance carries price pressure that is not yet complete (Chordia & Subrahmanyam 2004; order-flow imbalance drives price linearly, Cont, Kukanov & Stoikov 2014). Perp twist, fixed a priori: flow that comes with a stretched perp premium in the same direction is leveraged chasing (crowded, prone to exhaustion), so it is excluded. Flow with a normal or opposite premium is kept, since it is more likely hedged or informed and persistent.
direction_choice: Continuation, chosen from Chordia & Subrahmanyam before any data. The contrary crypto evidence (15m reversal conditioned on flow, AUC ~0.54, arXiv 2608.21888) is at a shorter horizon and is noted as the main threat.

sources.summary: Chordia & Subrahmanyam (2004, JFE 72, 485-518): with order splitting, imbalances are autocorrelated; lagged imbalances relate positively to returns, reversing sign once the current imbalance is controlled for; imbalance strategies earn significant returns in 1988-98 NYSE daily data. Daily equities, older microstructure; a Taiwan replication finds no lagged predictability.

Short-horizon mean reversion in crypto (2026, arXiv): signs Binance bars with kline taker-buy volume and finds 15m reversal conditioned on flow, out-of-sample AUC ~0.54; lagged imbalance adds nothing out of sample. EVIDENCE AGAINST continuation at short horizons.
Net buying pressure in bitcoin options (2021, arXiv): hourly/daily order imbalance shows no clear predictive effect on spot in the excerpt read. Weak or no prior support.

Not the closed ES/NQ order-flow absorption zones (price-level zones from footprint prints). No crypto rows in data_spend_ledger for these families.
data_choice: Taker flow from kline taker_buy_volume (the metrics taker ratio is empty Jan-May 2022). BTC and ETH train 2020-01 -> 2024-06 (premium index from 2020-01; residual gaps make hours skip). SOL report-only from 2022-05.

rules.hours: completed UTC hours [h, h+1h); decision at the close of the 1m bar opening h+59m (time h+1h). An hour counts only with 60 bars and 0 stale bars.
rules.flow: imb_h = (2 * sum taker_buy_volume - sum volume) / sum volume over the hour's 60 bars (in [-1, 1]).
rules.premium: prem_h = mean of the Binance premium-index 1m closes for bars opening in [h, h+1h); needs >= 50 of 60 rows, else the hour is invalid.
rules.scale: z_flow and z_prem = (x_h - mean) / std (ddof 1) over the previous `lookback` valid hours (720 = 30 days); need >= min_hist (480). The hour joins the history after it is used.
rules.signal: |z_flow| >= Z; side = sign(z_flow); skip if side * z_prem >= prem_cap (1.0), i.e. the premium is already stretched in the flow's direction.
rules.bracket: market entry at the next 1m open. Stop = max(1.0 * daily ATR(14) of the last completed UTC day, 1.5% of the decision close). No target. Time exit 12h after entry. Mirror-flat book.

walk_forward: fixed: no parameter selected. Both Z are judged by the frozen train gate (BTC and ETH both must pass). Passing configs go to validation; K counts candidates sent.
expected_trades: |z| >= 2 on ~5% of hours (fat tails may add more), minus the premium filter, about 1 signal/day; with a 12h mirror-flat hold roughly 800-1,200 trades per asset over 4.5 years. Z = 3 roughly a fifth of that (~200-300). Unknown before running.
costs_note: ATR(14) stops are 4-5% median (K1/K2): at a 12h hold, cost about 0.02R (7.6 bp RT plus 0.5 day of swap). At the 1.5% floor, about 0.06R.
report_not_gate: net R long vs short (bull drift, see K1/K2), by year, and with the premium filter's skipped signals counted; share of time vs stop exits.
rejection_evidence: Reject if the frozen train gate fails for both Z on BTC or ETH. Count against it (report): a pass from one side only, or a weaker result at Z = 3.
